elements.quote: However, there is uncertainty about which grade school children are more likely susceptible to and transmit SARS-CoV-2 in schools.
elements.reason: Describes important uncertainties in the current knowledge about SARS-CoV-2 transmission in schools.

elements.quote: This living systematic review summarizes the most recent evidence to understand SARS-CoV-2 transmission in schools and includes a study quality assessment to aid interpretation.
elements.reason: Explains the importance and need for conducting the review to understand transmission and aid interpretation.

elements.quote: Our previous review suggested lower IAR and SARS-CoV-2 positivity rate in students compared to school staff [4], whereas in this update when we combined studies from the second and first update we found higher IAR in students when compared to school staff.
elements.reason: Identifies and cites the previous review, explaining the need for the current update.
The review is not focused on intervention effects; it assesses SARS-CoV-2 transmission in schools, not evaluating specific interventions.
The review does not involve complex interventions or a logic model; it focuses on transmission rates without hypothesised relationships between intervention components and outcomes.

elements.quote: We updated a living systematic review and meta-analysis to investigate the extent of SARS-CoV-2 transmission in schools.
elements.reason: Explicit statement of the review objective

elements.quote: We performed parallel review of titles, abstracts, and subsequently full texts based on updated inclusion and exclusion criteria following the population, exposure, comparison, outcome (PECO) approach... We included children (defined as ≤18 years old) who were attending school, and their close contacts... We excluded home-schooled children and their close contacts, and schools with student numbers below 20. For study outcomes, we included infections traced to a school index case with a COVID-19 positive test. We updated inclusion criteria of study types to include: 1) Cohort studies... 2) Cross-sectional studies... 3) Pre-post studies...
elements.reason: Explicitly specifies study characteristics including PECO framework, eligible study designs, settings, and follow-up requirements.

elements.quote: We included articles in peer-reviewed journals and pre-prints, and excluded comments, conference abstracts and interviews.
elements.reason: Publication status is specified, but language and dissemination year are not mentioned as eligibility criteria.
No distinction is made between exclusion because outcomes were not measured and exclusion because outcome results were not reported in the eligibility criteria or exclusions described.

elements.quote: We found 11 cohort studies [13-17,24-29] that investigated secondary infection attack... and one cross-sectional studies [18] that investigated SARS-CoV-2 positivity compared to community rates.
elements.reason: Groups used in synthesis (cohort and cross-sectional studies) are specified and linked to the comparisons (secondary infection attack vs. community rates) as per the review objectives.
No rationales are provided for notable restrictions on study eligibility, such as excluding schools with fewer than 20 students or requiring comparison with community rates.

elements.quote: Based on our new inclusion and exclusion criteria 12 studies were retained in our review: 1 st update: n = 6 (cohort studies [13-17] and cross-sectional studies [18-23]; 2 nd update: n = 6 (cohort studies [24-29]) ( Figure 1 ) and the characteristics of the included studies are presented in Tables 1-4 . We found 11 cohort studies [13-17,24-29] that investigated secondary infection attack ( Table 1 and Table 2 ) and one cross-sectional studies [18] that investigated SARS-CoV-2 positivity compared to community rates ( Table 3 and Table 4 ). Five cross-sectional studies [19-23] from our 1 st update that investigated SARS-COV-2 positivity but did not compare with community rates were excluded.
elements.reason: The quote explicitly describes the process of applying inclusion/exclusion criteria to decide eligibility for each synthesis, with studies categorized into cohort studies for secondary attack and cross-sectional studies for positivity compared to community rates, including exclusions based on criteria.

elements.quote: However, the following potential limitations should be considered. First, further interpretation of age-group differences in IARs and positivity rates could not be performed because most of the included studies did not provide the raw data of student ages and we could not unify different age groups to run the meta-analysis. [...] Second, cross-comparisons between IARs and positivity rates reported in different regions/countries is difficult because of differences in the sampling and testing methods used, timing of the studies in relation to the outbreak, response measures and underlying community transmission. [...] Third, seven studies in the included 12 studies (58.3%) reported prevention and control measures in place in schools [...] making it difficult to assess the effectiveness of NPIs under the school environment [...] Forth, only one cross-sectional study has compared positivity rate in schools and communities to assess the impact of school opening on transmission [...] Fifth, 25.0% (3/12) of included studies are pre-print publications and have not been peer-reviewed. For the majority of included studies there is high risk of bias and we should interpret the results with caution.
elements.reason: The discussion section explicitly lists five limitations of the included evidence, covering data availability, methodological heterogeneity, intervention reporting, comparative evidence, and study quality.

elements.quote: However, the following potential limitations should be considered.

elements.quote: Moreover, the differences may contribute to the heterogeneity observed in the meta-analyses results and raise methodological concerns around the validity of the meta-analysis.

elements.quote: Therefore, we suggest effective implementation of NPIs such as physical distancing, small-size class, cancellation of school mass gatherings, hand hygiene, and wearing of face masks, with school re-opening [1].

elements.quote: we suggest future studies could conduct sensitivity analyses for transmission rates in different school grades (child care/primary/sary) because this could provide evidence for the decision making of school closure and re-opening, with staggered class start and end times.

elements.quote: We suggest future research could compare positivity rates to evaluate whether SARS-CoV-2 is more easily to spread in school environment.
